items.title: A power of ten
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: What is $\log_{10} 0.001$?

feedback.generic: Write 0.001 as a power of 10. The logarithm is that power.

byKey.pos: You gave the power for 1,000. A thousandth is $10^{-3}$, so its power is negative.
byKey.zeros: You counted the two zeros after the point. $0.01 = 10^{-2}$; one more place gives $10^{-3}$.

explain.text: $0.001 = \tfrac{1}{1000} = 10^{-3}$. A logarithm asks for the power, so $\log_{10} 0.001 = -3$. Numbers between 0 and 1 have negative logarithms.

items.title: Order tickets
items.prose: An order ticket names one of 5 shares, buy or sell, and an order type. There are 3 types: market, limit and stop.
items.question: How many different tickets are there?

feedback.correct: Five shares, two sides, three types: $5 \times 2 \times 3 = 30$.
feedback.generic: Each ticket makes three choices in a row. Multiply the number of options for each.

byKey.add: You added the options, 5 + 2 + 3. Each share goes with every side and every type, so they multiply.
byKey.side: You left out buy or sell. That doubles the 15 share and type pairs.

explain.text: Every share can pair with either side, and each pair with any of three types. Choices made one after another multiply: $5 \times 2 \times 3 = 30$.

items.title: Round the rim
items.prose: A wheel of radius 4 cm turns through 2.5 radians.
items.question: How far does a point on the rim travel, in cm?

feedback.generic: In radians, the arc is the radius times the angle.

byKey.divide: You divided the angle by the radius. Each radian adds one radius of arc, so multiply.
byKey.add: You added the radius and the angle. Each radian adds one radius of arc, so multiply.
byKey.degrees: You treated 2.5 as degrees. The angle is already in radians, so $s = r\theta$ needs no conversion.

explain.text: One radian sweeps an arc as long as the radius, 4 cm. So 2.5 radians sweep $2.5 \times 4 = 10$ cm. That is $s = r\theta$.

items.title: Doubling terms
items.prose: A sequence starts 7, 14, 28, 56.
items.question: What is its 8th term?

feedback.generic: Find the common ratio. The 8th term is 7 steps after the first.

byKey.power-n: You used $2^8$. The first term has had no doublings, so term 8 has had 7.
byKey.times-n: You multiplied 7 by 2 and then by 8. The ratio is applied once per step, so it is a power.

explain.text: Each term doubles the one before, so $r = 2$. The 8th term is 7 doublings after 7: $u_8 = 7 \times 2^{7} = 7 \times 128 = 896$.

items.title: Four falls in a row
items.prose: A share price falls 3% a day for 4 days in a row.
items.question: Which gives the price now as a multiple of the starting price?

options.why: You took 3% of the starting price four times. Each fall is 3% of a smaller price.
You raised the fall to the power 4. The part kept each day is 0.97, not 0.03.
You multiplied by 4. Four days in a row multiply four factors of 0.97.

feedback.correct: Each day keeps 97% of the day before, so four days give $0.97^4 \approx 0.885$.
feedback.generic: Turn the 3% fall into a factor, then apply it once a day.

explain.text: A 3% fall leaves $1 - 0.03 = 0.97$ of the price. Four falls multiply four of those factors: $0.97^4 \approx 0.8853$. That is a fall of about 11.5%, a little less than 12%.

items.title: Roots and reciprocals
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: What is $27^{2/3} \times 16^{-1/4}$?

feedback.generic: A denominator in the power is a root. A minus sign in the power is a reciprocal.

byKey.negative: You read $16^{-1/4}$ as −2. A negative power gives a reciprocal, not a negative number.
byKey.no-flip: You found the fourth root, 2, but kept it. The minus sign in the power turns it into $\tfrac12$.

explain.text: The cube root of 27 is 3, and squaring gives 9. The fourth root of 16 is 2, and the minus sign makes it $\tfrac12$. So $9 \times \tfrac12 = 4.5$.

items.title: Saving a bit more each week
items.prose: You save £20 in week 1, £25 in week 2, and £5 more each week after that.
items.question: How much have you saved in total after 30 weeks, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Find the amount saved in week 30 first, then pair the first and last weeks.

byKey.last: You took week 30 as $20 + 30 \times 5$. Week 30 is only 29 steps after week 1.
byKey.flat: You saved £20 every week. The amount rises by £5 each week.
byKey.term: You found the amount for week 30 alone. The question asks for all 30 weeks added up.

explain.text: Week 30 is 29 steps after week 1: $20 + 29 \times 5 = 165$. Pairing week 1 with week 30, week 2 with week 29 and so on gives 15 pairs of £185. That is $15 \times 185 = 2775$.

items.title: Two vans from one depot
items.prose: Two straight roads leave a depot at $60^\circ$ to each other. One van drives 5 km along one road; a second drives 8 km along the other. Work without a calculator.
items.question: How far apart are the vans, in km?

feedback.correct: $c^2 = 25 + 64 - 40 = 49$, so the vans are 7 km apart.
feedback.generic: The angle is not a right angle. Use the cosine rule with the angle between the two known sides.

byKey.pythag: You used Pythagoras, $\sqrt{89}$. That needs a right angle; here the angle is $60^\circ$.
byKey.plus: You added the $2ab\cos C$ term. The cosine rule subtracts it.

explain.text: The cosine rule gives $c^2 = 5^2 + 8^2 - 2 \times 5 \times 8 \cos 60^\circ$. With $\cos 60^\circ = \tfrac12$ this is $89 - 40 = 49$. So $c = 7$.

items.title: Waiting for £8,000
items.prose: £5,000 earns 6% a year, added once a year. You may use a calculator.
items.question: After how many whole years does the balance first go above £8,000?

feedback.correct: $n = \ln 1.6 / \ln 1.06 \approx 8.07$, so the balance passes £8,000 in year 9.
feedback.generic: Solve $5000 \times 1.06^n = 8000$ with logs, then think about whole years.

byKey.floor: You rounded 8.07 down. After 8 years the balance is still £7,969.24, below £8,000.
byKey.simple: You added £300 a year. Interest is paid on the interest too, so it gets there sooner.

explain.text: Dividing by 5000 gives $1.06^n = 1.6$, so $n = \dfrac{\ln 1.6}{\ln 1.06} \approx 8.07$. After 8 years the balance is £7,969.24, just short. After 9 it is £8,447.39.

items.title: Growing all the time
items.prose: £2,000 grows at a continuous rate of 5% a year for 4 years. You may use a calculator.
items.question: What is it worth then, to the nearest penny?

feedback.generic: Continuous growth uses $Pe^{rt}$.

byKey.annual: You added 5% once a year, $2000 \times 1.05^4$. A continuous rate compounds all the time: use $e^{rt}$.
byKey.simple: You added £100 a year. Growth is on the growing amount, so it compounds.

explain.text: With continuous growth the value is $Pe^{rt} = 2000e^{0.05 \times 4} = 2000e^{0.2}$. That is £2,442.81. Paying 5% once a year would give a little less, £2,431.01.

items.title: A daily cycle
items.prose: A desk’s message rate rises and falls through the day. The graph shows it, in thousands a minute, against hours after midnight.
items.question: Which equation fits the graph?

options.why: You used the period, 12 hours, as the number inside. The period is $2\pi / b$, so $b = \pi / 6$.
You took the trough-to-peak height, 6, as the amplitude. The amplitude is half of it.
That wave repeats every 24 hours. The graph repeats every 12.

feedback.generic: Read the midline, the amplitude and the time for one full cycle.

explain.text: The graph runs between 2 and 8, so the midline is 5 and the amplitude 3. Peaks at 3 and 15 hours put the period at 12. A period of 12 needs $b = 2\pi / 12 = \pi / 6$.

items.title: Odd numbers in a sigma
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: What is $\displaystyle\sum_{k=4}^{15} (2k - 1)$?

feedback.generic: Count the terms from $k = 4$ to $k = 15$, then find the first and last.

byKey.count: You counted $15 - 4 = 11$ terms. Both ends are included, so there are 12.
byKey.from-one: You started at $k = 1$. This sum starts at $k = 4$, so 1, 3 and 5 are left out.

explain.text: There are $15 - 4 + 1 = 12$ terms, from 7 up to 29. Pairing first with last gives 6 pairs of 36, so the sum is 216. Check: $1 + 3 + \dots + 29 = 15^2 = 225$, minus $1 + 3 + 5 = 9$.

items.title: Sitting together
items.prose: Six traders sit in a row of six desks. Two of them, Priya and Tom, must sit next to each other.
items.question: How many seatings are there?

feedback.correct: Glue Priya and Tom into one block: $5! \times 2 = 240$.
feedback.generic: Treat the pair as one block, then count the ways inside the block.

byKey.no-swap: You arranged the five blocks but kept Priya on the left. Tom can sit on either side of her.
byKey.all: You counted every seating, $6!$. Most of those split Priya and Tom.

explain.text: With Priya and Tom glued together there are 5 blocks to arrange: $5! = 120$ ways. Inside the block they can sit either way round. That doubles it to 240.

items.title: Every solution
items.prose: Solve $\cos 2x = \tfrac12$ for $0^\circ \le x < 360^\circ$.
items.question: Select all that apply: which values of $x$ are solutions?

options.why: You solved $\cos x = \tfrac12$. At $x = 60^\circ$, $2x = 120^\circ$, where cosine is $-\tfrac12$.
You used $180^\circ + 60^\circ$ for $2x$. Cosine is negative there: $\cos 240^\circ = -\tfrac12$.
You solved $\cos x = \tfrac12$. At $x = 300^\circ$, $2x = 600^\circ$, the same as $240^\circ$.

feedback.generic: Let $u = 2x$. Since $x$ runs up to 360°, $u$ runs up to 720°.

explain.text: Put $u = 2x$, so $u$ runs from 0° to 720°. $\cos u = \tfrac12$ at 60° and 300°, and again 360° later at 420° and 660°. Halving gives 30°, 150°, 210° and 330°.

items.title: One term of a bracket
items.prose: Expand $(2 - x)^6$.
items.question: What is the coefficient of $x^3$?

feedback.generic: The $x^3$ term picks $-x$ from 3 brackets and 2 from the other 3.

byKey.sign: You dropped the minus. The term holds $(-x)^3 = -x^3$, which is negative.
byKey.binom-only: You gave $\binom{6}{3}$ alone. Each of the other three brackets gives a 2, so multiply by $2^3$.
byKey.binom-sign: You kept the sign but left out $2^3$. The three brackets that give 2 multiply the term by 8.

explain.text: The general term is $\binom{6}{k} 2^{6-k} (-x)^k$. With $k = 3$ it is $20 \times 8 \times (-1) x^3 = -160x^3$. The minus sign survives because 3 is odd.

items.title: Two tech shares
items.prose: A watchlist holds 10 shares, 4 of them tech. You pick 3 at random, every set of 3 equally likely.
items.question: What is the chance that exactly 2 are tech? Give a decimal.

feedback.generic: Count the sets with 2 tech and 1 other, then divide by all sets of 3.

byKey.other: You counted the tech pairs but not the third share. Each pair goes with any of the 6 others.
byKey.replace: You treated the picks as independent, with 0.4 each time. Picking without putting back changes the odds.
byKey.one-order: You counted one order: tech, tech, other. The other share can come first, second or third.

explain.text: There are $\binom{10}{3} = 120$ sets of 3. Two tech from 4 is $\binom42 = 6$ ways and one other from 6 is 6 ways. That gives $36 / 120 = 0.3$.

items.title: Three days of log returns
items.prose: A share’s daily log returns over three days are 0.04, −0.07 and 0.01. You may use a calculator.
items.question: What is the simple return over the three days, as a decimal to four places?

feedback.generic: Add the log returns, then turn the total back into a simple return.

byKey.sum: You stopped at the sum of the log returns. Turn it back with $e^{x} - 1$.
byKey.compound: You compounded them as simple returns. Log returns add; you then need $e^{x} - 1$.

explain.text: Log returns add: $0.04 - 0.07 + 0.01 = -0.02$. That is $\ln(P_3 / P_0)$, so $P_3 / P_0 = e^{-0.02} \approx 0.9802$. The simple return is $-0.0198$.

items.title: Length of a combination
items.prose: $\mathbf{u} = (3, -1)$ and $\mathbf{v} = (2, 4)$.
items.question: What is $|2\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v}|$? Give two decimal places.

feedback.generic: Build the vector first, component by component, then use Pythagoras.

byKey.mags: You worked out $2|\mathbf{u}| - |\mathbf{v}|$. Lengths do not subtract; build the vector first.
byKey.plus: You added $\mathbf{v}$. The question takes it away.
byKey.abs-sum: You added the sizes of the parts, 4 and 6. A length uses Pythagoras: $\sqrt{4^2 + 6^2}$.

explain.text: $2\mathbf{u} = (6, -2)$, and subtracting $\mathbf{v}$ gives $(4, -6)$. Its length is $\sqrt{16 + 36} = \sqrt{52} \approx 7.21$. Lengths do not subtract: $2|\mathbf{u}| - |\mathbf{v}|$ is only 1.85.

items.title: Signs from the quadrant
items.prose: An angle $\theta$ lies between $180^\circ$ and $270^\circ$, and $\cos\theta = -\tfrac{8}{17}$.
items.question: What is $\tan\theta$? Give a decimal.

feedback.generic: Use $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$, and choose the sign of sine from the quadrant.

byKey.sign: You took sine as positive. Between 180° and 270° the point is below the axis, so sine is negative too.
byKey.sine: You stopped at $\sin\theta$. Divide it by $\cos\theta$ to get the tangent.

explain.text: $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \tfrac{64}{289} = \tfrac{225}{289}$, and sine is negative between 180° and 270°: $-\tfrac{15}{17}$. Then $\tan\theta = \dfrac{-15/17}{-8/17} = 1.875$. Both are negative, so tangent is positive there.

items.title: A difference of logs
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: Solve $\log_3 (x + 6) - \log_3 x = 2$.

feedback.generic: Combine the two logs into one with the quotient law, then undo the log.

byKey.cube: You used $2^3 = 8$. Undoing $\log_3$ of a number equal to 2 gives $3^2 = 9$.
byKey.double: You used $3 \times 2 = 6$. Undoing the log raises 3 to the power 2, which is 9.

explain.text: The quotient law gives $\log_3 \tfrac{x + 6}{x} = 2$, so $\tfrac{x + 6}{x} = 3^2 = 9$. Then $x + 6 = 9x$ and $x = \tfrac68 = 0.75$. Check: $\log_3 6.75 - \log_3 0.75 = \log_3 9 = 2$.

items.title: Paid today and every year
items.prose: A fund pays £60 today and £60 on the same date every year after, forever. Money is discounted at 4% a year.
items.question: What is the whole stream worth today, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Write the values as a geometric series with ratio $\tfrac{1}{1.04}$, starting with today’s £60.

byKey.today: You valued the payments from next year on. Today’s £60 is worth £60 and must be added.
byKey.minus: You took today’s £60 away. It is paid now, so it adds to the value.
byKey.ratio: You used 0.04 as the ratio. Each year’s value is the last one divided by 1.04.

explain.text: The values are $60 + \tfrac{60}{1.04} + \tfrac{60}{1.04^2} + \dots$, a geometric series with $r = \tfrac{1}{1.04}$. Its sum is $\dfrac{60}{1 - 1/1.04} = \dfrac{60 \times 1.04}{0.04} = 1560$. That is today’s £60 plus £1,500 for the rest.

items.title: A third of the way
items.prose: $\vec{OA} = \mathbf{a}$ and $\vec{OB} = \mathbf{b}$. X lies on AB with $AX : XB = 1 : 2$.
items.question: Which vector is $\vec{OX}$?

options.why: You measured the third from B. X is a third of the way from A, so it sits nearer A.
You wrote $\vec{AB}$ as $\mathbf{a} - \mathbf{b}$. A vector from A to B is end minus start: $\mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a}$.
You took a third of $\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b}$. That point is on the line from O to the parallelogram’s far corner, not on AB.

feedback.generic: Go from O to A, then a third of the way along $\vec{AB}$.

explain.text: $\vec{AB} = \mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a}$, and X is a third of the way along it. So $\vec{OX} = \mathbf{a} + \tfrac13(\mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a})$. Collecting terms gives $\tfrac23\mathbf{a} + \tfrac13\mathbf{b}$.

items.title: Codes with a repeat
items.prose: A broker’s account code has 4 characters. Each is a digit from 0 to 9 or a letter from A to F, and characters may repeat.
items.question: How many codes have at least one character repeated?

feedback.correct: All codes minus those with four different characters: $65536 - 43680 = 21856$.
feedback.generic: Count what you do not want, codes with no repeat, and take it from the total.

byKey.distinct: You counted codes with four different characters. Those are the ones to take away.
byKey.all: You counted every code. Some have four different characters and must be taken away.

explain.text: There are 16 characters, so $16^4 = 65536$ codes. Those with four different characters number $16 \times 15 \times 14 \times 13 = 43680$. The rest, 21856, repeat at least one character.

items.title: When two accounts meet
items.prose: Account A holds £1,000 growing at a continuous 5% a year. Account B holds £1,200 growing at a continuous 3% a year. You may use a calculator.
items.question: After how many years are they worth the same? Give two decimal places.

feedback.generic: Set $1000e^{0.05t} = 1200e^{0.03t}$ and gather the exponentials on one side.

byKey.add: You added the rates. Dividing $e^{0.05t}$ by $e^{0.03t}$ subtracts the powers, leaving $e^{0.02t}$.
byKey.simple: You grew each account by a fixed amount a year. Continuous growth compounds, so use $e^{rt}$.

explain.text: Dividing both sides by $1000e^{0.03t}$ gives $e^{0.02t} = 1.2$. Taking $\ln$: $0.02t = \ln 1.2 \approx 0.1823$, so $t \approx 9.12$ years. Each account is then worth about £1,577.

items.title: Paying off a loan
items.prose: You borrow £10,000 and repay it with 10 equal payments, one at the end of each year. Interest is 5% a year. You may use a calculator.
items.question: What is each payment, to the nearest penny?

feedback.correct: The payments’ values today must add to £10,000: $P = \dfrac{500}{1 - 1.05^{-10}} \approx$ £1,295.05.
feedback.generic: Value each payment today and add them as a geometric series. Set the total equal to £10,000.

byKey.no-interest: You split £10,000 into ten parts. That ignores the interest on what is still owed.
byKey.simple: You charged 5% of £10,000 every year. The balance falls as you pay, so the interest falls too.
byKey.future: You grew the whole loan for 10 years, then split it. Early payments cut the balance, so less interest builds up.

explain.text: Payment $k$ is worth $P / 1.05^k$ today, so the ten add to $P \cdot \dfrac{1 - 1.05^{-10}}{0.05}$. Setting this equal to 10000 gives $P = \dfrac{10000 \times 0.05}{1 - 1.05^{-10}} \approx 1295.05$. Check: paying £1,295.05 a year clears the balance after year 10.
